open_points.subject: OwnerFormField facts
open_points.text: The row gives the field's name, its path in the owner request or its values, with a tuple's position marked;
open_points.question: Is `path` a separate fact of OwnerFormField, or is the complete path represented only by `name`?
options: `name` is the complete path-bearing fact; there is no separate path fact
`name` is a display or transport name derived from a separate path fact
open_points.default_guess: Treat `name` as the complete path-bearing fact and add no separate path fact.

witness.initial: An owner request contains a nested field whose path is `customer.name`.
events: The release author declares the owner form row.
The owner page emits the field and the owner interface reads it back.
outcomes: One implementation stores only the path-bearing name in OwnerFormField.
Another stores a field name and a separate structured path in OwnerFormField.
witness.observer: The release author and the owner-interface implementation see different model facts and equality.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField tuple path
open_points.text: the field's name, which holds its path and the mark of each tuple position in it, so that two rows of different paths are different rows;
open_points.question: What semantic fact does a tuple-position mark carry: a concrete tuple index, a schema-level positional slot, or merely the fact that a path component traverses a tuple?
options: The concrete zero-based position is part of the path fact
A schema-level tuple slot is part of the path fact
Only a tuple-traversal marker is part of the path fact
open_points.default_guess: Make the concrete tuple position part of the path fact; leave only its encoding to a later state.

witness.initial: A request has a tuple with two members of the same scalar type.
events: The release declares a row targeting the first member and another targeting the second.
outcomes: An implementation records positions 0 and 1, so the rows have different facts.
An implementation records only a generic tuple marker, so the paths cannot distinguish the two members.
witness.observer: The owner-interface reader assigns submitted text to different request members.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField product-action scope
open_points.text: A row of the owner form table: one field an owner page writes into a form or a query, and the owner interface reads back (owner, 2026-11-25).
open_points.question: How is a row associated with the owner product action, page, form, or query that uses it, and is that association a fact of OwnerFormField or an enclosing catalogue key?
options: OwnerFormField carries an action or form identifier as a fact
OWNER_FORM_FIELDS is partitioned by action or form outside each row
Every row belongs to one global form-field namespace and applies wherever its path matches
open_points.default_guess: Partition OWNER_FORM_FIELDS by owner action outside the row, keeping the action out of OwnerFormField's value identity.

witness.initial: Create-project and correct-customer pages both contain a path-bearing field named `name`.
events: The release declares both pages' rows.
Each page renders its own form and reads a submission.
outcomes: One implementation keys the catalogue by product action and selects the correct row set.
Another treats OWNER_FORM_FIELDS as one global row set and applies both matching rows.
witness.observer: The owner sees different fields rendered or the server reads a submission into a different request.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField member value kind
open_points.question: For a row whose value kind is `member`, what determines the particular enumeration whose member value is accepted, and is that enumeration reference a fact of OwnerFormField?
options: Each `member` row carries the target enumeration as a fact
The target enumeration is inferred from the destination request path's declared type
All `member` rows use one shared enumeration vocabulary
open_points.default_guess: Infer the target enumeration from the declared type at the destination path and do not add an enumeration-reference fact.

witness.initial: One owner form has a project-status member field and a customer-kind member field.
events: The page submits the text `active` for the status field and `person` for the customer-kind field.
The owner interface reads both rows.
outcomes: An implementation resolves a different enumeration from each destination path.
Another has no per-row or path-derived enumeration and uses a shared member domain.
witness.observer: The owner-interface reader accepts different member values and constructs different request facts.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField source and minting
open_points.question: Which named component or actor authors or derives the OwnerFormField values, and from what authoritative facts is OWNER_FORM_FIELDS produced?
options: Release authors explicitly declare the rows and the data provider only supplies them
The data provider derives the rows from owner request models or contracts
The owner-interface implementation constructs the rows from its pages
open_points.default_guess: Treat explicitly release-authored rows as authoritative and have the data provider expose them unchanged.

witness.initial: A new owner request field is added to a release.
events: The release and owner interface are assembled.
outcomes: An explicitly maintained OWNER_FORM_FIELDS table remains unchanged until its author adds a row.
A generated OWNER_FORM_FIELDS table acquires the row automatically from the changed request contract.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether the new field is rendered and read in that release.

open_points.subject: Owner form carrier
open_points.text: Owner form carrier: `request`, `values` — what an owner form field fills, the owner request itself or the values it carries (M29).
open_points.question: Must Owner form carrier be a runtime `kind: enum` model or read-only `kind: vocabulary` spec-data model?
open_points.default_guess: Use `kind: enum` because the closed scalar members type a runtime OwnerFormField fact.

witness.initial: State 6 closes the model representation for OwnerFormField.
events: The compiler receives the Owner form carrier declaration.
Generated code uses the carrier type in OwnerFormField.
outcomes: As an enum, the generated runtime model has a closed carrier type.
As a vocabulary, the declaration is read-only spec data and does not become the same runtime type.
witness.observer: Contract authors and generated-code consumers see different model kinds and runtime types.

open_points.subject: Owner form value kind
open_points.text: Owner form value kind: `text`, `integer`, `boolean`, `member` — how an owner form field's text is read: as itself, as an integer's decimal digits, as `true` or `false`, or as an enumeration member's value (M29).
open_points.question: Must Owner form value kind be a runtime `kind: enum` model or read-only `kind: vocabulary` spec-data model?
open_points.default_guess: Use `kind: enum` because the closed scalar members type a runtime OwnerFormField fact.

witness.initial: State 6 closes the model representation for OwnerFormField.
events: The compiler receives the Owner form value kind declaration.
Generated code uses the value kind in OwnerFormField.
outcomes: As an enum, the generated runtime model has a closed value-kind type.
As a vocabulary, the declaration is read-only spec data and does not become the same runtime type.
witness.observer: Contract authors and generated-code consumers see different model kinds and runtime types.
